task_row_model.query: In the 2023 multicenter randomized trial of the NeuRelief device, what were the eligibility criteria, sample size per arm, primary outcome measure and assessment timepoint, follow-up duration, and the pre-specified statistical significance level?

documents.content: Background: The 2023 NeuRelief multicenter randomized controlled trial enrolled adults with chronic neuropathic pain to evaluate an implantable modulation device. Methods: Between January and November 2023, 240 participants were randomized 1:1 across 12 centers (120 per arm). The study specified the primary endpoint as the change in average weekly pain intensity from baseline assessed at 12 weeks. Secondary assessments continued to 24 weeks to capture durability. The trial protocol included standardized device implantation and blinded pain diaries. Historical notes on neuromodulation advances were provided as context alongside technical device descriptions.
documents.reasoning_trace: Contains enrollment numbers (240 total, 1:1 randomization, 120 per arm), primary endpoint timing (12 weeks), and overall follow-up to 24 weeks; background material is tangential.

documents.content: Press summary: Investigators recruited patients who had persistent neuropathic pain for at least six months and reported baseline average pain of 4/10 or greater on the 11-point Numerical Rating Scale (NRS). Inclusion required prior failure of at least two pharmacologic therapies for neuropathic pain. The primary outcome was pre-specified as change from baseline in average weekly NRS pain score, analyzed at the 12-week primary timepoint. Statistical analysis was planned with a two-sided alpha of 0.05. Commentary noted enthusiasm for symptom relief but also cautioned about generalizability; speculative quotes from investigators were included.
documents.reasoning_trace: Provides eligibility criteria (≥6 months duration, baseline NRS ≥4/10, prior failure of ≥2 meds), defines primary outcome measure (weekly average NRS change at 12 weeks) and alpha=0.05; includes speculative press quotes as noise.

documents.content: Lab memorandum: Screening logs show eligible ages were 18 to 75 years. Exclusion criteria listed in trial screening included active local or systemic infection, presence of an implanted pacemaker or other incompatible electronic device, and pregnancy or nursing. The sample size decision noted logistical planning for 240 randomized subjects; investigators jotted that power calculations and recruitment feasibility drove the 1:1 allocation target. The note also contains a short unrelated case summary of a single-patient compassionate-use implant and a glossary entry contrasting terms "neuropathic" and "nociceptive" pain.
documents.reasoning_trace: Lists age range (18–75) and exclusions (infection, pacemaker, pregnancy); confirms sample size planning for 240 and 1:1 allocation; unrelated case study and glossary are noise.

documents.content: Reference entry: The 11-point Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) is commonly used in pain research; patients rate pain from 0 (no pain) to 10 (worst imaginable). Neuropathic pain arises from lesion or disease of the somatosensory system and has diverse prevalence estimates across populations. Methodological boilerplate often emphasizes intent-to-treat analyses and CONSORT reporting. Adjacent terminology such as "neuromodulation," "neurostimulation," and device-specific nomenclature is provided for reader orientation. The entry also recaps prior unrelated trials of spinal cord stimulation from the early 2000s as historical context.
documents.reasoning_trace: Defines NRS and provides methodological boilerplate and historical/contextual material; serves as background noise rather than trial-specific facts.

task_row_model.golden_answer: Eligibility: adults 18–75 with chronic neuropathic pain ≥6 months, baseline average pain ≥4/10 on the 11-point NRS, and prior failure of at least two pharmacologic therapies; exclusions included active infection, implanted pacemaker, and pregnancy. The multicenter RCT randomized 240 participants 1:1 (120 per arm). Primary outcome was change from baseline in average weekly NRS pain at 12 weeks (primary endpoint); two-sided α = 0.05; overall follow-up to 24 weeks.
